title: Research: exact Q8 pair minima under unit-priced inverse labels (complete r=2 census, no compression)
body:
## Summary

Complete finite group-algebra census in the formal `F2[Q8]` register model at
`r = 2`: every one of the 64 ordered diagonal pair targets `diag([g1],[g2])`
costs exactly its direct bill, both with **unit-priced inverse labels**
`x = i`, `x^-1 = -i`, `y = j`, `y^-1 = -j` (24 paid factors) and under the
positive-label baseline `{x, y}` (12 paid factors). Unit-priced inverse
labels therefore enable no cross-register sharing compression; they change
only the re-pricing of the elements `-i`, `-j` from three calls to one. No
kappa, supplier, frontier or multiplication-theorem claim.

Package: `research/q8-inverse-label-pair-census/`. Contributor: **Aaron
Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent
human review claimed).

## Scope and changed premise

This answers open question 1 of the merged predecessor
`research/q8-central-commutator-pair`
(https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1822): "does a label set
including the inverses compress any pair target?", extended from its two named
endpoints to the complete pair family, with the positive-label pair table as
the comparison baseline.

* Roles: exactly `r = 2`, both registers arbitrary dirty inputs, endpoint
  restored exactly. Every factor `D_N(g) = I + ([g]+1)N` is charged
  (`N = u v^T` binary rank-one idempotent, `v^T u = 1` mod 2; six `N`).
  No free address maps, no COPY/ERASE, no clean ancilla.
* Free scalar `GL_2(F2)` mixing is normalized by augmentation; conjugation
  closure of the idempotent list is rechecked for all six `S` in `GL_2(F2)`.
* Acceptance is equality in every coefficient of the eight-element group
  algebra `F2[Q8]` (a uniform identity on arbitrary dirty inputs), never a
  finite-column test.
* The factor set is closed under inversion: `D_N(g) D_N(g^-1) = I`, checked
  for every factor of both alphabets.

## Exact result

Rows index the first target entry, columns the second, order
`1, -1, i, -i, j, -j, k, -k`. In both alphabets `minimum = direct bill` for
all 64 pairs (`compressed_inv=0`, `compressed_pos=0`):

```text
inverse labels (min = bill)          positive labels (min = bill)
     1  -1   i  -i   j  -j   k  -k       1  -1   i  -i   j  -j   k  -k
 1   0   2   1   1   1   1   2   2    1   0   2   1   3   1   3   2   2
-1   2   4   3   3   3   3   4   4   -1   2   4   3   5   3   5   4   4
 i   1   3   2   2   2   2   3   3    i   1   3   2   4   2   4   3   3
-i   1   3   2   2   2   2   3   3   -i   3   5   4   6   4   6   5   5
 j   1   3   2   2   2   2   3   3    j   1   3   2   4   2   4   3   3
-j   1   3   2   2   2   2   3   3   -j   3   5   4   6   4   6   5   5
 k   2   4   3   3   3   3   4   4    k   2   4   3   5   3   5   4   4
-k   2   4   3   3   3   3   4   4   -k   2   4   3   5   3   5   4   4
```

| Fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Pairs checked per alphabet | 64 (all ordered pairs in `Q8`) |
| Pairs compressed below their bill | 0 (inverse), 0 (positive) |
| Pairs whose minimum changes between alphabets | 28 (exactly those with `-i` or `-j` as an entry) |
| Maximum minimum | 4 (inverse), 6 (positive) |
| Predecessor endpoints reproduced | `diag([z],[z])` = 4, `diag([xy],[yx])` = 4 (positive alphabet) |

Every difference between the two tables is the re-pricing of `-i`, `-j`
(length 3 to 1 per entry), not sharing.

## Evidence

`python -I -B research/q8-inverse-label-pair-census/verify.py` (stdlib only,
about 40 s) recomputes everything and compares with `CERTIFICATE.json`:

* Q8 group laws exhaustively (512 associativity triples, `x^2 = y^2 = z`,
  `xy = k`, `yx = -k`, `z` central, `[x,y] = z`) and agreement of two
  independently built group tables.
* Idempotent completeness (6 of 9 binary pairs), `GL_2(F2)` conjugation
  closure, `D_N(g)^2 = D_N(g^2)` and the inverse identity for all factors.
* Complete BFS layers and ball SHA-256 digests from two independent engines
  (bitmask convolution from a `(sign, axis)` quaternion table vs frozenset
  convolution from explicit Hamilton 4-tuple integer products), agreeing on
  every layer and ball: inverse `[1, 24, 358, 4104]` (depth at most 3),
  positive `[1, 12, 110, 936, 6945, 48080]` (depth at most 5).
* Calibration with the merged predecessor: its recorded positive-alphabet
  layers `[1, 12, 110, 936]` and its two endpoint minima are reproduced
  exactly (source pinned in `SOURCES.json`).
* All 128 attaining words replay coefficientwise in both engines; 372
  single-call omission controls miss their targets; one mutated-target
  control fails; known-distance controls (`1` at 0, `diag([i],[1])` at 1,
  `diag([z],[1])` at 2); alphabet monotonicity holds for all 64 pairs.

Complete shorter-word exclusion is the BFS itself: every word of length at
most 3 (inverse) or at most 5 (positive) lies in the complete ball, and no
ball contains a target below the recorded minimum.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/q8-inverse-label-pair-census/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/q8-inverse-label-pair-census --check-only
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'
```

Observed on this branch (CPython 3.12 and 3.13, Windows):

```text
PASS_Q8_INVERSE_LABEL_CENSUS pairs=64 inv_layers=[1, 24, 358, 4104] pos_layers=[1, 12, 110, 936, 6945, 48080] compressed_inv=0 compressed_pos=0 omission_controls=372 no_new_kappa
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
Ran 65 tests in 25.030s  OK (skipped=3)
```

## Limitations and unrun obligations

* Scoped to these two alphabets, `r = 2`, and these 64 targets. It is not an
  impossibility theorem for other alphabets, `r >= 3`, or the rational-frame
  model. No written structural lower bound is claimed; the minima rest on the
  complete search.
* No supplier mapping, paid reserve, moment or kappa change; the `a < D/E`
  diagnostic does not apply (no candidate improvement is priced).
* Not a proof-assistant verification: two independent Python engines and
  finite exhaustions; no Lean or native C++ replay. The `r >= 3` extension
  and a second-order lower bound are recorded as open questions in the
  package README.
* Hosted CI checks were pending at submission time.

## Overlap and predecessor credit

  `research/bit-dihedral-commutator`
  (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1443); the selected
  Q8 pair result `research/q8-central-commutator-pair`
  (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1822), whose open
  question 1 this closes. Register-model lineage: Ali Romman
  (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/468), Gareth Davidson
  (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1333),
  `research/bit-three-register-lower-bound`.
* Concurrent work this is deliberately distinct from: the `r = 3` three-role
  positive-label minima (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2248,
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2243) and the
  one- and two-factor words for `diag(i,j,k)` with all-nonidentity labels
  (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2303,
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2300). The
  predecessor's open question 2 (`diag([z],[z],[z])` at `r = 3`) is not taken,
  to avoid that concurrent object.
* `scripts/find_overlap.py` refreshes at 2026-10-15T04:34Z and before
  submission (complete pagination) found no inverse-label Q8 pair object.
